local: Es ya libre, ya libre este suelo,
english: [[Bolivians]], a propitious fate
has at long last crowned our vows and longings;
This land is free, free at last.
Its servile state has now finally ceased.

local: Al estruendo marcial que ayer fuera
y al clamor de la guerra horroroso,
dulces himnos de paz y de unión.
english: The martial turmoil of yesterday,
and the horrible clamor of war,
are followed today, in harmonious contrast,
by sweet hymns of peace and unity.

local: De la Patria, el alto nombre,
Y en sus aras de nuevo juremos:
english: Let us keep the lofty name of our Fatherland
in glorious splendor.
And, on its altars, once more we must swear:
To die before we would live as slaves!

local: Loor eterno a los bravos guerreros,
english: To die before we would live as slaves!
To die before we would live as slaves!
Eternal praise to the brave warriors
whose heroic valor and firmness

local: Que sus nombres, en mármol y en bronce,
english: conquered the freedom and glories that now
a happy [[Bolivia]] justly begins to enjoy!
Let their names, preserved forever in marble and bronze,
transmit their glory to remote future ages.

local: Aquí alzó la justicia su trono
english: And in resounding songs let them repeat:
Freedom! Freedom! Freedom!
Here has Justice erected its throne
which vile oppression ignores

local: y en su timbre glorioso legose
que ha debido a Bolívar su nombre
english: and, on its glorious laurel it bequeathed us
Freedom, freedom, freedom
This innocent and beautiful land,
which owes its name to Bolívar,

local: es la patria feliz donde el hombre
goza el bien de la dicha y la paz.
english: is the happy homeland where mankind
enjoys the benefits of bliss and peace.
If a foreigner may, any given day
even attempt to subjugate [[Bolivia]],

local: Que los hijos del grande Bolívar
han ya mil y mil veces jurado:
english: let him prepare for a fatal destiny,
which menaces such haughty aggressor.
For the sons of the mighty Bolívar
have sworn, thousands upon thousands of times:

local: de la Patria el augusto pendón.
english: to die rather than see the country's
majestic banner humiliated.
